plans.note: Section 15 is captioned 'Limitation of Garman's Liability', suggesting a one-sided cap; check the cap amount, whether it is mutual, and whether IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct are carved out.

Section 13 is an express IP indemnity from Garman. Confirm scope (defence and settlement, replace/refund options), absence of unreasonable conditions on us, and that no broad reverse indemnity from Sparkling appears; check interaction with the sec-15 cap.

A software licence of this type rarely restrains the customer's business. Scan sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 (General Matters) for any covenant limiting products we may buy or build before concluding absent.
Check the grant (sec-2), maintenance (sec-10) and fees (sec-11) for any sole-source or exclusive-supplier language; otherwise treat as absent — no obligation on us to source solely from Garman.
Look in fees and maintenance pricing for any most-favoured-customer language. An MFN running in our favour would be beneficial and must not be flagged; only an MFN burdening Sparkling is a deviation.

Section 19 expressly covers non-solicitation of employees. Check mutuality, duration, whether it is limited to personnel involved in the engagement, and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicants are carved out; note any survival via sec-18.

Section 17 (Term and Termination) is primary; sections 7 and 8 (option to reject software) give an early exit at acceptance. Assess whether Sparkling may terminate on notice without penalty and whether Garman has a broader convenience right or can suspend maintenance.

Maintenance terms typically auto-renew annually; check sec-10 and sec-17 for the renewal mechanic and notice window, and sec-11 for any uncapped price uplift on renewal (uplift cap absence is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation).

Governing law, venue and any dispute-resolution/arbitration provision will sit in Section 20 (General Matters). Given the Canadian/US parties, a provincial or state law other than the accepted list would be a deviation; an accepted-but-not-preferred law is only a rationale note.

Assignment clause expected in Section 20; also check sec-2/sec-3 for transfer restrictions on the licence. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger, and that Garman has no termination right on our change of control.

Ownership of the software sits with Garman (sec-2/sec-3), which is expected; focus on our data (sec-4 data conversion), any assignment to Garman of our modifications, feedback or configurations, and escrowed materials (sec-16). Confidentiality (sec-14) covers our data protection.

Section 2 is the grant; test whether it extends to affiliates, authorized locations (see sec-1 definitions/schedules) and outsourced contractors, and whether it is perpetual/irrevocable or revocable at will. Section 3 restrictions may narrow the scope.
Licence-verification audit rights, if any, would appear in sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) or sec-20. If present, check notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost; otherwise mark absent.

Look for late-payment interest, early-termination charges or stipulated damages payable by Sparkling in sec-11 and sec-17. Service credits or remedies running to us are beneficial and should not be flagged.

Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty) is primary; acceptance testing (sec-6) and maintenance (sec-10) supply the remedy path. Check warranty duration from acceptance, conformance to specifications, remedy (repair/replace/refund) and any disclaimer of implied warranties read with sec-15.

No insurance heading appears in the outline; check sec-20 (General Matters) and the on-site implementation provisions (sec-4, sec-9) for any certificate-of-insurance requirement before recording as missing.

Check sec-11 fees and sec-10 maintenance for any committed number of users/locations, minimum annual spend or obligation to keep paying maintenance for a fixed period without exit; schedules referenced in sec-1 may carry volumes.

Section 17 likely requires return/destruction of software on termination; look for any reciprocal obligation to return our data and provide migration assistance. Source code escrow (sec-16) and the rejection/refund mechanic (sec-8) are partial substitutes but not a transition-services clause.
